brief.situation: You are the cloud engineer on call for Fernbrook Outdoor, a fictional shop. At 10:00 a pipeline deployed revision r42 of the Cloud Run service checkout with all traffic. At 10:05 the alert fires: checkout errors. The SLO is 99.9% availability over the day.
handover: Yesterday's revision r41 is still in the service with no traffic.
The pipeline deploys with the default settings: a new revision takes all traffic.
howItWorks: The board shows the service, its traffic split and its revisions; meters show errors, today's availability and orders charged in the sandbox.
Each task takes your time: start it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. Deploys finish later on the same clock.
When you close the incident, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Checkout takes about 40 orders a minute at this hour.

How many minutes each command or task takes, and when the fictional problem spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. Building and deploying a revision with --no-traffic takes 10 minutes.

writeup.question: For the record: how you found the bad revision, how you restored service, and how the fix went out safely.

parts.label: Find it
parts.criteria: Uses metrics split by revision to tie the errors to r42, and the logs for the cause (a wrong environment variable), before changing traffic.
parts.modelAnswer: Errors by revision showed 8% 500s on r42 only, from 10:00; the logs showed PAYMENTS_URL pointing at localhost.

parts.label: Restore
parts.criteria: Moves traffic back to the last good revision with update-traffic (immediate) rather than rebuilding or adding instances, and relates it to the error budget.
parts.modelAnswer: update-traffic r41=100 restored service at once; rebuilding would have taken 15 more minutes of a 99.9% budget that allows about 1.4 minutes of full outage a day, and more instances of r42 only fail faster.

parts.label: Ship the fix
parts.criteria: Deploys with --no-traffic and a tag, tests the tag URL, then a small canary before 100%; notes that the test caught the second config error.
parts.modelAnswer: r43 went out with --no-traffic --tag canary; a test order on the tag URL showed it charging the sandbox. r44 fixed that, passed the tag test, took 10% for ten minutes, then 100%.

expertPath.text: Errors by revision: r42 only. update-traffic r41=100: service restored at once.
Logs: PAYMENTS_URL wrong. Deploy r43 with --no-traffic --tag canary; a test order on the tag URL charges the sandbox.
Deploy r44 tagged, test it, send 10% for ten minutes, then 100%.

shipped.headline: Good: back at once, fixed safely
shipped.body: You let the metrics name the revision, used traffic to restore service in seconds of the error budget, and shipped the fix in steps that caught a second mistake before any customer saw it.

shippedGaps.headline: Restored, with gaps
shippedGaps.body: Service is back. The criteria show what cost budget, what was skipped in the rollout, or what the record gets wrong.

budgetBlown.headline: The budget ran out
budgetBlown.body: At 8% errors, a 99.9% day allows about 18 minutes. The previous revision was one update-traffic command away.

stillBroken.headline: Still failing
stillBroken.body: r42 still serves. More instances of a bad revision fail faster; moving traffic is the fix.

uncharged.headline: An untested revision took real orders
uncharged.body: Deploying with all traffic, or canarying an untested revision, sent customers to a build that charged the sandbox. --no-traffic with a tag lets you test first.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Request counts by revision show 8% 500s on r42 only, since its 10:00 deploy. update-traffic --to-revisions r41=100 restores service immediately, inside a 99.9% error budget that allows about 1.4 minutes of full outage a day (18 minutes at 8%); a rebuild takes 15 minutes and more instances only fail faster. The logs show a wrong PAYMENTS_URL. Deploy the fix with --no-traffic --tag canary and test the tag URL: r43 charged the sandbox, so r44 fixes that, passes the test, takes 10% for ten minutes, then 100%.
